title: Solve globally
summary: Use later sentences and the words left in the bank to check and change earlier choices.

sections.title: An answer can change
content: Think of a time you changed your mind after reading further. A word that looks right at the first gap may be wrong once you read the ending.
In a word bank, each choice also uses up a word. A wrong early choice can leave you with no good word for a later gap.

sections.title: Three passes through the text
content: First pass: read the whole text and ask how the story starts, what changes and how it ends. Do not fill any gap yet.
Second pass: fill the gaps you are sure about. Each word you use makes the bank smaller, so the harder gaps get easier.
Third pass: read the full text again with your words in place. If a later sentence does not agree with an earlier choice, go back and change it.

sections.title: Let the ending decide
content: Take this text: ‘Dewi felt ___ on the way to the stage. Her hands were shaking. After the song, the crowd cheered and she felt ___.’ The bank has ‘proud’ and ‘anxious’. Both could fit the first gap if you stop reading there.

The next sentence, ‘Her hands were shaking’, points to ‘anxious’. The cheering at the end points to ‘proud’. If you had put ‘proud’ first, you would have only ‘anxious’ left for the end, and that would not make sense.
So when the last gap looks wrong, the mistake may be earlier. Check earlier gaps before you change the last one.

sections.title: Fill the sure gaps first
content: Read the whole text. Mark the gap you are most sure about and fill it first. Then see what is left in the bank.

sections.title: Check the whole text
content: These texts have two words that can both seem right at one gap. Only one arrangement works for the whole text.
Use all three passes, and read the complete text once more before you submit.

sections.title: Find where it went wrong
content: Stopped too soon: I chose a word without reading what came after it. Used up a word: I used a word early that a later gap needed. Did not go back: I saw a problem at the end but did not check earlier choices.
Grammar or meaning error: the mistake was at that one gap, so use the checks from the last two lessons.

sections.title: Try a new story
content: Complete one unseen story with eight gaps. You will see your feedback only after you answer every gap. If you need more practice, you will get a new story.
